gel_data_resources  (read-only)
===================

Outputs of the Genomics England bioinformatics pipelines and other resources,
mounted on the desktop (~/gel_data_resources) and the HPC (/gel_data_resources).

  main_programme/        100,000 Genomes Project datasets (by type, then date)
  gms/                   NHS Genomic Medicine Service datasets
  pilot/                 pilot programme datasets
  example_config_files/  configuration templates for R, Python and the LabKey API
  example_scripts/       example scripts (LabKey API queries, workshops)
  workflows/             pipelines provided for researchers

This folder is read-only. Writing here gives "Permission denied": to unpack a
file, write the output elsewhere, e.g.  gunzip -c file.gz > ~/re_gecip/.../file

[Training simulator: the large datasets are not included. Practicals add the
files they need.]

Configuration templates.

Desktop:   cd $HOME && cp -rf ~/gel_data_resources/example_config_files/Workspaces/. .
HPC:       cp -rf /gel_data_resources/example_config_files/Double_Helix/. ./

Then edit ~/.netrc: put your username (initial + last name, e.g. jdoe) and your
RE password in place of yourusername / yourPasswordHere, and make the file
private:   chmod 600 ~/.netrc
The LabKey API reads your credentials from ~/.netrc.

bcftools plugins – a small synthetic example
============================================

Training simulator: these files are synthetic. They describe no real person: a
made-up family (child, father, mother) and an unrelated sample, on a made-up
1,000-base chromosome "chr1". They come from the genomics-wasm project
(https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, datasets/hts/common/, MIT
licence), which uses them to check its builds of bcftools.

  trio-csq.vcf   12 variants of four samples, with VEP-style annotations in the
                 CSQ field (Allele|Consequence|IMPACT|SYMBOL|Gene|Feature|...),
                 missing, haploid and multiallelic genotypes, and Mendelian errors
  phased.vcf     the same samples, with phased genotypes
  family.ped     the pedigree of the trio

Try (module load bcftools/1.21 first; the folder is read-only, so write any
output into your own folder):

  D=/gel_data_resources/example_scripts/workshop_scripts/bcftools_plugins
  bcftools +split-vep $D/trio-csq.vcf -l
  bcftools +split-vep $D/trio-csq.vcf -d -f '%CHROM\t%POS\t%Consequence\t%SYMBOL\n'
  bcftools +fill-tags $D/trio-csq.vcf -Ov -o ~/filled.vcf -- -t AN,AC,AF
  bcftools +mendelian2 $D/trio-csq.vcf -P $D/family.ped -m c
  bcftools +trio-switch-rate $D/phased.vcf -- -p $D/family.ped

Relatedness – kinship with PLINK 2 (KING-robust) on a small synthetic cohort
===========================================================================

Training simulator: the genotypes here are synthetic – no real person. They come from the genomics-wasm project
(https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, datasets/king/, MIT licence), which made them to check its builds:
104 of its 105 samples, 32,809 SNPs on chromosomes 1 to 4. The folder is read-only: write your results into your own
folder.

  cohort.bed, .bim, .fam   the genotypes (PLINK 1 binary files). The .fam declares one family, FAM: DAD, MOM and
                           their children CHILD1 and CHILD2. Every other sample is a family of its own: DUP (family
                           COPY) and U01 … U99
  truth.txt                how the samples are really related: look at it after step 2
  run_relatedness.sh       steps 2 and 4 as a job for the HPC (LSF)

Genomics England computed the relatedness of its aggregated genomes (aggV2, aggV3) the same way: PLINK 2's KING-robust
kinship for every pair, a table of the pairs at 0.0442 or more (third degree or closer), and --king-cutoff 0.0442 for a
list of unrelated participants. In the Research Environment, aggV2's are in
/gel_data_resources/main_programme/aggregation/aggregate_gVCF_strelka/aggV2/additional_data/PCs_relatedness/relatedness
(not in this simulator).

  module load plink2/2.0.0-b.1-dev
  D=/gel_data_resources/example_scripts/workshop_scripts/relatedness
  mkdir -p /re_gecip/training/$USER/relatedness && cd /re_gecip/training/$USER/relatedness

1. The kinship of every pair of samples – 104 samples, 5,356 pairs:

  plink2 --bfile $D/cohort --make-king-table --out cohort
  head -3 cohort.kin0
      NSNP     the SNPs where both samples have a genotype
      HETHET   the share of them where both are heterozygous
      IBS0     the share where they have no allele in common (one is AA, the other aa)
      KINSHIP  the KING-robust kinship coefficient
  sort -k8,8gr cohort.kin0 | head          the most related pairs first

2. Only the related pairs – third degree or closer – and what they are:

  plink2 --bfile $D/cohort --make-king-table --king-table-filter 0.0442 --out related
  awk 'NR > 1 { k = $8; d = k > 0.354 ? "duplicate or identical twin" : k > 0.177 ? "1st degree" : k > 0.0884 ? "2nd degree" : "3rd degree"; print $2, $4, k, $7, d }' related.kin0

      kinship  above 0.354      the same genome: a sample twice, or identical twins (0.5)
               0.177 - 0.354    first degree: parent and child, or full siblings (0.25)
               0.0884 - 0.177   second degree: grandparent, aunt or uncle, half sibling (0.125)
               0.0442 - 0.0884  third degree: first cousins (0.0625)
      IBS0 tells the first degree apart. A child has one allele from each parent, so a parent and child always share
      an allele: their IBS0 is about 0. Full siblings can inherit different alleles: their IBS0 is above 0.

  Which pairs are parents and children, which are siblings? Is a pair related that the .fam does not declare?
  cat $D/truth.txt

3. Check the pedigree – only the pairs within each family of the .fam (FID):

  plink2 --bfile $D/cohort --make-king-table rel-check --out within
  cat within.kin0                          DAD and MOM: kinship about 0, as the founders of a pedigree should be

4. A list of unrelated samples, as Genomics England made for aggV2, with the cutoff 0.0442:

  plink2 --bfile $D/cohort --king-cutoff 0.0442 --out unrelated
  cat unrelated.king.cutoff.out.id         the samples left out, so that no two of the rest are related
  wc -l unrelated.king.cutoff.in.id        the samples kept (and a header line)
  awk 'NR == FNR { keep[$2]; next } FNR > 1 && ($2 in keep) && ($4 in keep) && $8 >= 0.0442' unrelated.king.cutoff.in.id cohort.kin0 | wc -l
                                           the related pairs among the samples kept: 0
  Analyses that assume unrelated people, such as association tests, keep only these: --keep unrelated.king.cutoff.in.id

As a job on the HPC (from your folder there):  bsub < $D/run_relatedness.sh

The 105th sample of genomics-wasm's cohort, U100, is left out because this build of PLINK 2 has a fault: with an odd
number of samples, its KING-robust values for the pairs of the first sample are wrong. The terminal says so when that
happens (man plink2).

  COPY DUP     FAM DAD      parent and child         0.2465    0
  COPY DUP     FAM MOM      parent and child         0.2494    0
  COPY DUP     FAM CHILD2   full siblings            0.2502    0.0216
  FAM DAD      FAM MOM      unrelated               -0.0069    0.0857

DUP is CHILD1 a second time, under another family ID: in a real cohort, a sample sequenced twice, a participant
recruited twice, or identical twins. So DUP is also DAD's and MOM's child and CHILD2's sibling, which the .fam does
not say.

Every other pair is unrelated: kinship near 0 (from -0.020 to 0.016 here). U01 … U99 are unrelated founders. U20 has
a fifth of its genotypes missing, so its pairs have fewer SNPs (NSNP 26,174 instead of 32,809). The full siblings
share both, one or neither of their parents' copies of a stretch of chromosome, in turn, in blocks of about 10 Mb.

Repeat expansions – ExpansionHunter and REViewer, with small example data
=========================================================================

Training simulator: the files here are small examples from the genomics-wasm project
(https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, datasets/repeats/), which checks its builds of ExpansionHunter
5.0.0 and REViewer 0.2.7 with them. The folder is read-only: write your results into your own folder.

  synthetic/                 a made-up sample – no real person: reads on artificial 8,000-base contigs, each with a CAG
                             repeat at 4,001-4,036 (twelve units in the reference)
                               NORMAL_CAG    chr1   12 and 18 units
                               EXPANDED_CAG  chr2   12 and 75 units – longer than a read (150 bases)
                               X_CAG         chrX   18 units: a male sample has one X (use --sex male)
                             catalog.json: the three loci; truth.json: the counts the reads were made from
  expansionhunter_example/   ExpansionHunter's own example (its repository, release 5.0.0; Apache 2.0, LICENSE.txt):
                             an SNV next to a CAG repeat. expected.vcf and expected.json are the results in that
                             repository, written by an earlier version: the same genotypes (SNV 0/1, CAG 2/10), some
                             counts and the header differ
  reviewer_example/          REViewer's own test input (its repository, release 0.2.7; GNU GPL 3, LICENSE.txt): the
                             BAMlet of the 1000 Genomes sample HG00684 at BEAN1, its VCF and catalog. reference.fa.gz is
                             chromosome 16 of hg38 with only the bases within 2,000 of the catalog's loci kept (the rest
                             is N; reference-mask.json lists them) – for this example only

The workflow (copy the lines into the terminal; the job script run_expansionhunter.sh does the same on the HPC):

  module load ExpansionHunter/5.0.0 samtools/1.21 REViewer/0.2.7
  D=/gel_data_resources/example_scripts/workshop_scripts/repeat_expansions
  mkdir -p /re_gecip/training/$USER/repeats && cd /re_gecip/training/$USER/repeats

1. Genotype the repeats (the reads, the reference and the catalog; the BAM needs its .bai, the reference its .fai):

  ExpansionHunter --reads $D/synthetic/reads.bam --reference $D/synthetic/reference.fa \
      --variant-catalog $D/synthetic/catalog.json --sex male --output-prefix synthetic
  ls                                       synthetic.vcf, synthetic.json, synthetic_realigned.bam
  grep -v '^##' synthetic.vcf | cut -f1,2,5,10
      GT:SO:REPCN:REPCI:… – REPCN: the repeat count of each allele; REPCI: its confidence interval. An allele longer
      than the reads is estimated: EXPANDED_CAG's long allele comes out near 75, with an interval around it.
  cat $D/synthetic/truth.json              the counts the reads were made from

2. Sort and index the reads ExpansionHunter used (the BAMlet: synthetic_realigned.bam is not sorted):

  samtools sort -o synthetic.sorted.bam synthetic_realigned.bam && samtools index synthetic.sorted.bam

3. Draw them – a picture for each locus, and the allele depths and phasing:

  REViewer --reads synthetic.sorted.bam --vcf synthetic.vcf --reference $D/synthetic/reference.fa \
      --catalog $D/synthetic/catalog.json --locus EXPANDED_CAG --output-prefix synthetic
  firefox synthetic.EXPANDED_CAG.svg       (or double-click it in the file manager)
  cat synthetic.metrics.tsv synthetic.phasing.tsv
  (--locus NORMAL_CAG,EXPANDED_CAG,X_CAG draws all three)

The reads in their alignments to the reference – the long allele's extra CAGs as insertions, and clipped reads –
are in IGV:

  igv -g $D/synthetic/reference.fa $D/synthetic/reads.bam chr2:3900-4150

(The BAMlet's reads carry their alignments to ExpansionHunter's repeat graph in tags, for REViewer: IGV shows them
as unmapped.)

REViewer's own example – BEAN1, 17 and 17 TGGAA units:

  REViewer --reads $D/reviewer_example/BEAN1_HG00684.bam --vcf $D/reviewer_example/HG00684.vcf \
      --reference $D/reviewer_example/reference.fa.gz --catalog $D/reviewer_example/catalog.json \
      --locus BEAN1 --output-prefix HG00684
  firefox HG00684.BEAN1.svg

ExpansionHunter's own example – an SNV and a repeat in one locus (REViewer 0.2.7 cannot draw such a locus):

  ExpansionHunter --reads $D/expansionhunter_example/variants.bam --reference $D/expansionhunter_example/reference.fa \
      --variant-catalog $D/expansionhunter_example/variants.json --output-prefix example
  grep -v '^##' example.vcf; grep -v '^##' $D/expansionhunter_example/expected.vcf

As a job on the HPC (from your folder there):  bsub < $D/run_expansionhunter.sh

#!/bin/bash
#BSUB -q short
#BSUB -P re_gecip_training
#BSUB -J expansionhunter
#BSUB -o expansionhunter.%J.out
#BSUB -e expansionhunter.%J.err
#BSUB -R "rusage[mem=2000]"
#
# ExpansionHunter, samtools and REViewer on the synthetic sample of this folder (see README.txt).
# Submit it from your own folder on the HPC – the results are written there:
#   cd /re_gecip/training/$USER/repeats
#   bsub < /gel_data_resources/example_scripts/workshop_scripts/repeat_expansions/run_expansionhunter.sh

module load ExpansionHunter/5.0.0 samtools/1.21 REViewer/0.2.7

D=/gel_data_resources/example_scripts/workshop_scripts/repeat_expansions/synthetic

ExpansionHunter --reads $D/reads.bam --reference $D/reference.fa \
    --variant-catalog $D/catalog.json --sex male --output-prefix synthetic

samtools sort -o synthetic.sorted.bam synthetic_realigned.bam
samtools index synthetic.sorted.bam

REViewer --reads synthetic.sorted.bam --vcf synthetic.vcf --reference $D/reference.fa \
    --catalog $D/catalog.json --locus NORMAL_CAG,EXPANDED_CAG,X_CAG --output-prefix synthetic

grep -v '^##' synthetic.vcf | cut -f1,2,5,10
cat synthetic.metrics.tsv

aggV2 principal components, ancestry and relatedness
===================================================

aggV2_PCs_ancestry_relatedness.tsv
  participant_id, platekey  the genome
  PC1 .. PC20               principal components computed on unrelated genomes
                            (one per pair closer than third degree removed),
                            relatives projected onto them
  pred_EUR .. pred_AMR      probability of each 1000 Genomes superpopulation
  ancestry0_8               the superpopulation with probability above 0.8
                            (NA when none reaches it)
  unrelated_set             1 = in the maximal set of unrelated genomes

relatedness/  PLINK 2 KING-robust kinship on high-quality common autosomal SNPs
  make_king_table.kin0                         pairs with kinship >= 0.0442
  assign_relatedness.king.cutoff.in.id/.out.id  the unrelated set (--king-cutoff 0.0442)

Kinship of about 0.5 means duplicate samples (or monozygotic twins),
0.25 first-degree relatives, 0.125 second-degree, 0.0625 third-degree.

aggV2 common-variant extract (PLINK 1 binary)
=============================================

aggV2_common_variants_extract.bed/.bim/.fam

Genotypes of every main programme germline genome (rare disease participants,
their relatives and cancer participants) at a set of common and low-frequency
SNPs on the autosomes and chromosome X, extracted from aggV2 (GRCh38).

  .fam   FID and IID are the plate keys (platekey in LabKey tables such as
         aggregate_gvcf_sample_stats, plated_sample and sequencing_report);
         sex is the participant's recorded sex (1 = male, 2 = female);
         the phenotype column is missing (-9).
  .bim   variant IDs are chr:pos:ref:alt; the counted allele (A1, column 5) is
         the ALT allele.

No sample or variant QC has been applied: missing calls, SNPs out of
Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, sequencing-batch differences, related and
duplicated samples are all still present.

Principal components, ancestry and relatedness for the same genomes:
  ../PCs_relatedness/aggV2_PCs_ancestry_relatedness.tsv
  ../PCs_relatedness/relatedness/   (PLINK 2 KING-robust, cut-off 0.0442)

reference.fa is two windows of chromosome 21 of the human reference GRCh38, from UCSC (hg38). truth.vcf holds records
of the SEQC2 high-confidence somatic SNV and indel truth set v1.2.1.

These are publicly distributed research data. Please cite:

  Fang LT, Zhu B, Zhao Y, et al. Establishing community reference samples, data and call sets for benchmarking
  cancer mutation detection using whole-genome sequencing. Nature Biotechnology 2021; 39: 1151-1160.
  doi:10.1038/s41587-021-00993-6

The files were prepared – the reads of two windows, moved onto the windows, nothing else changed – by the genomics-wasm
project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, commit bfacba3: datasets/strelka2/hcc1395), whose
manifest records every source, byte range and step. Where every file came from, and its SHA-256: provenance.json
(in the workbench's data/examples/somatic).


Training simulator: these files come from the Bioinformatics workbench's example data
(comparativechrono/bioinformatics-workbench, data/examples/somatic). They are public data
of the cell lines HCC1395 (tumour) and HCC1395BL (normal) released by the SEQC2 consortium
- not data of any Genomics England participant. In the simulator the reads are delivered as
/genomes/by_date/2016-08-11/HX00100001/LP3000001-DNA_A01 (normal) and
/genomes/by_date/2016-08-11/HX00100002/LP3000002-DNA_B01 (tumour, with the somatic truth set
as its Variations/LP3000002-DNA_B01.somatic.vcf). The reference is two windows of
chromosome 21 (GRCh38): chr21_10572001_10582000 and chr21_21404501_21423500 - in IGV choose
the genome "GRCh38 chr21 windows (training)".
